research_question: In acutely ill hospitalized medical patients receiving venous thromboembolism prophylaxis, does extended-duration anticoagulation, compared with standard-duration anticoagulation, increase the risk of major bleeding within 45 days (short-term, primary analysis)?
control_label: Standard-duration anticoagulant thromboprophylaxis (or placebo after standard course)
outcome_description: Major bleeding events (as defined by each trial, typically ISTH criteria) occurring within 45 days of randomization (short-term), reported as number of patients with a major bleeding event and total randomized per arm. Primary-analysis population only (all randomized acutely ill medical patients), excluding COVID-19-only sensitivity analyses, same-extended-agent sensitivity analyses, and any subgroup analyses (sex, age, cancer history, D-dimer, infection status).
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR below 1 expressed in the favorable direction) means extended-duration anticoagulation produced FEWER major bleeding events than standard-duration anticoagulation; a negative effect means extended duration caused MORE major bleeding (the expected harm signal).
search_queries: extended duration thromboprophylaxis acutely ill medical patients randomized trial major bleeding
extended anticoagulation versus standard duration venous thromboembolism prophylaxis hospitalized medical patients trial
betrixaban rivaroxaban apixaban enoxaparin extended prophylaxis medically ill randomized controlled trial bleeding outcomes
inclusion_criteria: Studies of acutely ill hospitalized medical patients (including COVID-19 and other acute medical illness) receiving anticoagulant thromboprophylaxis
Compares an extended-duration anticoagulation regimen with a standard-duration regimen (or placebo/no anticoagulation after the standard course)
Reports quantitative bleeding outcome data, including number of major bleeding events and number randomized or analyzed per arm
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, narrative review, opinion piece, protocol, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)
No comparison between an extended-duration treatment arm and a standard-duration/control arm
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts/denominators, proportions, odds ratios, or means+SDs)

Completely unrelated to extended-duration anticoagulant thromboprophylaxis in acutely ill medical patients (e.g. surgical/orthopedic prophylaxis only, treatment of established VTE, atrial fibrillation stroke prevention)
moderators_to_extract: Anticoagulant class/agent used in the extended arm (DOAC vs LMWH)
Patient population (COVID-19 vs non-COVID acute medical illness)
Risk of bias / blinding (double-blind placebo-controlled vs open-label)
effect_size_note: Pool as a Risk Ratio using each trial's reported number of major bleeding events and total randomized per arm (intention-to-treat denominators where available), restricted to the short-term window (≤45 days) from the primary analysis population. Trials reporting zero major bleeding events in BOTH arms are "not estimable" for a ratio measure and should be excluded from pooling rather than continuity-corrected; single-zero-arm trials may use a standard continuity correction or Mantel-Haenszel pooling without correction. A higher event rate in the extended-duration arm reflects genuine harm, not an extraction error, because major bleeding is a safety outcome.
